mainTopic: Respect for תפילין: holding them in the bathroom, at meals, wrapping them with money, and placing them under one's head
overview: The amud opens with רב נחמן keeping hold of his תפילין because holding them protects a person. A ברייתא then forbids praying, urinating, or sleeping while holding תפילין, and שמואל adds that holding everyday objects also distracts from prayer. רב ששת says this ברייתא follows בית שמאי. The גמרא tries to defend him by reading the line 'what I permitted here, I forbade there' as being about how much of the body one uncovers. That defense fails, and רב ששת is refuted. The גמרא then explains that splashing drops make the makeshift bathroom stricter, and that the ברייתא's 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה' is a warning not to use that argument. Next come rules for a סעודת קבע: relieve yourself first, and take off your תפילין until ברכת המזון (רבי חייא says to put them on the table). The גמרא settles two ברייתות about wrapping תפילין with money by asking whether the cloth was set aside for them, and רב חסדא and אביי disagree about what that requires. Finally, שמואל allows תפילין under one's head even with his wife present. A ברייתא refutes him, yet רבא rules like שמואל, and his reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן would not hand over his תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רב נחמן let his students carry his book of אגדה but kept his תפילין, because he believed they would protect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...they will protect me.] רבא said: When we walked behind רב נחמן, if he was holding a book of אגדה he would give it to us to carry. If he was holding תפילין he would not give them to us. He said: Since the Sages allowed holding them, they will protect me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the previous statement ('they will protect me') and adds a matching story about רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a holy book was a burden he was happy to hand off to his students. תפילין were different: since the Sages allowed holding them, keeping them in hand was itself a source of protection, so he held on to them. This backs up the idea from just before this section.

phrases.english: they will protect me.
phrases.notes: This word ends the line right before this section: since the Sages allowed holding תפילין, they will guard me.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָזְלִינַן בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: When we would walk behind Rav Nachman,
when he was holding a book of aggadah
he would give it to us;
when he was holding tefillin
he would not give them to us;
he said: Since the Sages permitted them,
they will protect me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כִּי הֲוָה אָזְלִינַן בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the idea from the previous section that holding תפילין protects a person
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since holding תפילין is permitted, one may keep them in hand as a source of protection.

steps.title: No praying, urinating, or sleeping while holding תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists activities a person may not do while holding תפילין or a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person may not hold תפילין in his hand or a ספר תורה in his arm and pray. He may not urinate while holding them, and he may not sleep with them, neither a real sleep nor a short nap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three rules about holding holy objects: no praying, no urinating, and no sleeping while holding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying while holding them is a problem because worry about dropping them pulls your mind away from the prayer. Urinating and sleeping are about keeping the holy objects respected and safe. Pay attention to the urinating rule, because the next steps argue about it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A person may not hold tefillin in his hand
or a Torah scroll in his arm and pray.
And he may not urinate with them,
and he may not sleep with them,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שֵׁינַת קֶבַע וְלֹא שֵׁינַת עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: neither a set sleep nor a casual nap.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לֹא יֹאחַז אָדָם תְּפִילִּין בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from protection by תפילין to limits on holding them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not pray, urinate, or sleep while holding תפילין or a ספר תורה.

steps.title: שמואל adds everyday objects
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that holding a knife, money, a bowl, or a loaf of bread is just like holding תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A knife, money, a bowl, and a loaf of bread are just like them.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל stretches the ברייתא's first rule to cover ordinary objects too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These things are not holy, so his point is about distraction. If you hold them while praying, you will worry about dropping them and lose focus, just as with תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: like them, the same as them

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A knife, money, a bowl, and a loaf of bread
are just like them.
phrases.notes: He means for praying: holding these also distracts you from your prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: סַכִּין וּמָעוֹת וּקְעָרָה וְכִכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's prayer rule to everyday objects
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding a knife, money, a bowl, or bread during prayer is also not allowed, because of distraction.

steps.title: רב ששת: this ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that the הלכה does not follow the ברייתא, because it must be the view of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב ששת: The הלכה is not like this ברייתא, because it follows בית שמאי. If it followed בית הלל: they allow holding תפילין even in a permanent bathroom, so do we even need to ask about a makeshift bathroom (urinating)?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects the ברייתא's rule against urinating while holding תפילין and explains that it must follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, בית הלל allow holding תפילין in your hand in a permanent bathroom. Urinating is like a 'makeshift bathroom', which is a lighter case. If בית הלל allow the more serious case, they would surely allow the lighter one, so a ברייתא that forbids it cannot be בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה
a makeshift bathroom, here meaning urinating

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not arguing with all of the ברייתא's rules. His proof is built only on the urinating rule, which he compares to a makeshift bathroom.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
The halacha is not like this baraita,
because it is the view of Beit Shammai.
For if it were Beit Hillel —
now, if they permit a permanent bathroom,
is a makeshift bathroom even a question?!
phrases.notes: Earlier on the daf, בית הלל let you hold תפילין in your hand in a permanent bathroom. Urinating counts as the makeshift kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֵית הִלְכְתָא כִּי הָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the ברייתא from step 2 by tying it to בית שמאי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא forbidding urinating while holding תפילין follows בית שמאי, and the הלכה is not like it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole debate that follows about what בית הלל really hold for a makeshift bathroom.

steps.title: Challenge: 'What I permitted here, I forbade there'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the bathroom ברייתא showing that something allowed in a permanent bathroom is forbidden in a makeshift one. That only fits בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Things that I permitted to you here, I forbade to you there.' Isn't this talking about תפילין? That works if you say it is בית הלל: I permitted holding them here, in a permanent bathroom, and I forbade it there, in a makeshift bathroom. But if you say it is בית שמאי, they did not permit anything at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's reasoning, using a line from a ברייתא about the two kinds of bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line says something is allowed in one place and forbidden in another. Only בית הלל allow anything (holding תפילין in a permanent bathroom), so the line must follow בית הלל, and it shows that they forbid it in a makeshift bathroom. That breaks רב ששת's 'all the more so' argument: בית הלל can forbid urinating with תפילין, so the ברייתא in step 2 could be בית הלל after all.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well (according to one view)
they did not permit anything at all

steps.whatToRemember: The 'permitted here, forbidden there' line only makes sense for בית הלל, so בית הלל do forbid holding תפילין in a makeshift bathroom. That undercuts רב ששת's proof.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Things that I permitted to you here,
I forbade to you here.
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is a permanent bathroom and the second is a makeshift one. This line comes from a ברייתא about the two kinds of bathroom.

phrases.english: Is it not referring to tefillin?
It works well if you say it is Beit Hillel:
I permitted to you here, in the permanent bathroom,

phrases.aramaic: אָסַרְתִּי לְךָ כָּאן בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא עֲרַאי.
phrases.english: I forbade to you there, in the makeshift bathroom.
But if you say it is Beit Shammai,
they did not permit anything at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's claim that בית הלל would surely allow a makeshift bathroom
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's 'all the more so' reasoning that the ברייתא must be בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא line that allows something in a permanent bathroom and forbids it in a makeshift one can only follow בית הלל. So בית הלל do forbid holding תפילין in a makeshift bathroom.

steps.title: That line was really about how much to uncover
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the bathroom ברייתא line from Step 5 is not about תפילין. It is about uncovering one טפח or two טפחיים. It then quotes two ברייתות that seem to disagree on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that line was taught, it was about one handbreadth versus two handbreadths. One ברייתא says: when a person relieves himself, he uncovers one handbreadth behind him and two in front. Another ברייתא says: one handbreadth behind and nothing at all in front.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by saying the line quoted in Step 5 has nothing to do with תפילין. It then sets up two ברייתות about uncovering that the next steps will try to settle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 read 'what I allowed here I forbade there' as a rule about תפילין, which would fit בית הלל. Now the גמרא moves that line to a different topic: how much of the body may be uncovered. If the line is not about תפילין, Step 5 no longer proves anything against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a basic unit of measure

phrases.english: When that was taught,
it was about one handbreadth and two handbreadths.
As one ברייתא teaches:
When he relieves himself,
he uncovers one handbreadth behind him
and two handbreadths in front.
And another ברייתא teaches:
One handbreadth behind him
and in front, nothing at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא, לְעִנְיַן טֶפַח וְטִפְחַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5 by moving the quoted line to a different topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the subject of the quoted source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line 'what I allowed here I forbade there' was about holding תפילין in the bathroom, which would show the ברייתא follows בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is about how much one uncovers, so it says nothing about תפילין, and רב ששת stands.

steps.title: First suggestion: one is about urination, one about defecation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both ברייתות are about a man. One is about defecation, where nothing is uncovered in front. The other is about urination, where two טפחיים are uncovered in front.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that both ברייתות are about a man, and there is no contradiction: one is about defecation and the other is about urination?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first way to settle the two ברייתות from Step 6. It says they are talking about two different bathroom needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, uncovering in front is allowed for urination but not for defecation. That fits the line 'what I allowed here I forbade there.' The question opens with 'מאי לאו', which signals that this suggestion may be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Isn't it that both are about a man,
and there is no difficulty:
here it is about defecation,
and here it is about urination?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the two ברייתות quoted in Step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other about uncovering in front.
steps.terutzMaskana: One is about urination and one is about defecation (this is rejected in the next step).

steps.title: Rejecting the urination reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects Step 7. If a ברייתא were about urination, why would a person need to uncover a טפח behind him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? If it were about urination, why would he need to uncover a handbreadth behind him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from Step 7 with a simple logical point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות say to uncover a טפח behind. That is only needed for defecation. So neither ברייתא can be about urination, and the urination-versus-defecation split falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a sharp rejection)

phrases.english: And can you really think so?!
If it is about urination,
why do I need a handbreadth behind him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split proposed in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Uncovering behind makes no sense for urination, yet both ברייתות require it.

steps.title: New answer: one is about a man, one about a woman
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות are about defecation. The one with two טפחיים in front is about a man. The one with nothing in front is about a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both are about defecation, and there is no contradiction: this one is about a man, and that one is about a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first suggestion, the גמרא gives a new way to settle the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man uncovers in front because he may urinate at the same time. A woman does not need to. So the different amounts come from the body, not from the type of bathroom need.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings a new answer after a rejection)

phrases.english: Rather, both are about defecation,
and there is no difficulty:
this one is about a man,
and that one is about a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 7 with a new split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is urination versus defecation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is a man versus a woman, both during defecation.

steps.title: Then why call it a קל וחומר with no answer?
steps.stepSummary: If the difference is just man versus woman, the ברייתא's phrase 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה' makes no sense. That difference is simply the natural way things are.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what about the line taught there: 'This is a קל וחומר that has no answer'? What does 'has no answer' mean? That is just the natural way of things!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the man-versus-woman answer from Step 9 by pointing to how the ברייתא itself describes this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A קל וחומר with no answer' means logic would say one thing, yet the הלכה says another. That phrase only fits if the ruling is surprising. A man and a woman uncovering differently is not surprising at all, so the phrase does not fit Step 9's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
There is no answer to it; the logic seems strong, yet the הלכה goes the other way
The natural way of the matter

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה' does not mean a strong, winning argument. It means a logical argument the הלכה does not follow, even though we cannot refute it.

phrases.english: If so,
that which is taught about it:
'This is a קל וחומר that has no answer'
what does 'has no answer' mean?
That is simply the natural way of things!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the man-versus-woman answer of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 9: man versus woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the rule a surprising קל וחומר that has no answer, but a natural difference between men and women is not surprising at all.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about תפילין, so רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'uncovering' reading failed, the ברייתא must be about תפילין. רבא's claim in the name of רב ששת stands refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the ברייתא talking about תפילין? Then this is a refutation of what רבא said in the name of רב ששת. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the idea that the ברייתא is about uncovering the body. It goes back to saying the ברייתא is about תפילין, which means רבא's statement is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 to 10 tried to protect רבא by saying the ברייתא was not about תפילין at all. That effort failed in Step 10, because the man/woman difference does not fit 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה.' So the original reading returns, and רבא's claim that the ברייתא follows בית שמאי is knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that... (going back to the other option)
A refutation: a proof that an Amora's statement cannot stand
Tefillin, the leather boxes worn on the head and arm

steps.whatToRemember: When an אמורא's statement is shown to clash with a ברייתא and every way of saving it fails, the גמרא declares 'תיובתא': his statement is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is refuted here, but the ברייתא itself is not rejected. The גמרא keeps working to understand the ברייתא in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about תפילין,
phrases.notes: Meaning the ברייתא from Step 5 is really talking about holding תפילין in the bathroom.

phrases.english: and it is a refutation of רבא who said in the name of רב ששת.
phrases.notes: רבא had said, in רב ששת's name, that this ברייתא follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, תְּפִילִּין, וּתְיוּבְתָּא דְרָבָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת. תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 10's קשיא, which knocked out the last 'uncovering' reading. The גמרא returns to the תפילין reading and concludes that רבא is refuted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is about holding תפילין in a bathroom, and רבא's statement in the name of רב ששת is refuted.

steps.title: The ברייתא's logic seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the ברייתא is hard to understand. If holding תפילין is allowed in a regular bathroom, it should surely be allowed in a makeshift one.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, there is a difficulty. Now, if a regular bathroom is permitted, isn't a makeshift bathroom permitted all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא is about תפילין, the גמרא challenges its logic. A regular bathroom, used for the heavier act, is permitted, so a makeshift one, used only for urinating, should be permitted even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא permits holding תפילין in the regular bathroom and forbids it in the makeshift one. The גמרא argues the opposite with a כל שכן: the makeshift case is lighter, so it should be more permitted, not less.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; whatever the answer to the earlier issue
A makeshift, temporary spot used for urinating

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult:
now, a regular bathroom is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא עֲרַאי לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן!
phrases.english: isn't a makeshift bathroom permitted all the more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 settled that the ברייתא is about תפילין. This step questions the ברייתא's own logic under that reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling: permitted in a regular bathroom, forbidden in a makeshift one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כל שכן argument: the makeshift bathroom is the lighter case, so it should be at least as permitted as the regular one.

steps.title: The difference is the splashing drops
steps.stepSummary: In a regular bathroom there are no drops, so it is permitted. In a makeshift bathroom there are drops, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: in a regular bathroom, where there are no drops, they permitted it. In a makeshift bathroom, where there are drops, they forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a practical difference. When standing to urinate, drops splash, and that problem does not come up in the regular bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that the lighter act should always be more permitted. The answer shows a factor that works the other way: splashing drops in the makeshift bathroom. That factor makes the makeshift case stricter, so the ברייתא's ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (explaining a source)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא קָבוּעַ דְּלֵיכָּא נִיצוֹצוֹת, שָׁרוּ.
phrases.english: a regular bathroom, where there are no drops, they permitted.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא עֲרַאי דְּאִיכָּא נִיצוֹצוֹת, אָסְרִי.
phrases.english: A makeshift bathroom, where there are drops, they forbade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12's כל שכן challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a factual difference (splashing drops) that makes the seemingly lighter case stricter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The makeshift bathroom is the lighter case, so it should be more permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The makeshift bathroom has splashing drops, so holding תפילין there is forbidden.

steps.title: Then the קל וחומר does have a refutation
steps.stepSummary: If the drops explain the difference, why does the ברייתא say its קל וחומר 'cannot be refuted'? The drops are an excellent refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'it has no refutation'? This is an excellent refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 13. If there is a clear reason why the makeshift bathroom is stricter, the ברייתא should not call its reasoning unanswerable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls its argument a 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה,' a logic no one can answer. But the splashing drops from Step 13 are exactly such an answer, since they explain the difference between the two bathrooms. So the answer in Step 13 seems to clash with the ברייתא's own wording.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no refutation; it cannot be answered

phrases.english: If so, why does it say 'it has no refutation'?
phrases.notes: These words come from the ברייתא's phrase 'קל וחומר שאין עליו תשובה.'

phrases.english: It is an excellent refutation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 13's answer by testing it against the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's explanation that splashing drops make the makeshift bathroom stricter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the drops give a solid reason for the difference, then the קל וחומר can be refuted. That contradicts the ברייתא calling it 'שאין עליו תשובה.'

steps.title: The ruling comes from a reason, not from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is re-read. It means: learn this law from the reason (the drops), and do not use a קל וחומר, even though a קל וחומר would look airtight.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: derive this law from the reason given, and not from a קל וחומר. If you did try to derive it by a קל וחומר, it would be a קל וחומר that cannot be answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14 by explaining what the ברייתא's words really mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not claiming its קל וחומר is the true source of the law. It is saying: a קל וחומר would point the other way and would seem impossible to refute. But we ignore it, because the real reason (drops in a makeshift bathroom) decides the law.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא re-reads a text)
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
That has no answer against it

steps.whatToRemember: The law that one may not hold תפילין in a makeshift bathroom comes from a practical reason (drops). The 'irrefutable קל וחומר' is mentioned only to warn us not to use it here.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is using the קל וחומר to reach its ruling. It is telling you NOT to use it, even though it looks unbeatable.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא תֵּיתֵי לַהּ בְּתוֹרַת טַעְמָא,
phrases.english: Derive this matter by way of the reason,
phrases.notes: The 'reason' is the drops from step 13: a makeshift bathroom has them, a regular one does not.

phrases.english: and do not derive it by a kal vachomer,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אָתְיָא לַהּ בְּתוֹרַת קַל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: for if you were to derive it by way of a kal vachomer,

phrases.aramaic: זֶהוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו תְּשׁוּבָה.
phrases.english: that would be a kal vachomer with no refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by re-reading the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to use a קל וחומר as its source, which the drops would refute.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא learns the law from the reason (drops), and only mentions the קל וחומר as something not to rely on.

steps.title: Relieving oneself before a long meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that before a סעודת קבע one should walk a bit, relieve himself, and only then go in to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: someone who wants to go in to a set meal walks four אמות ten times, or ten אמות four times, relieves himself, and then goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new but related topic, bringing a ברייתא about going to the bathroom before a long meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The walking helps the body get ready to relieve itself. Doing this first means he won't have to leave in the middle of the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: A set, formal meal that lasts a while

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who wishes to enter a set meal
walks four cubits ten times,
or ten cubits four times,
and relieves himself, and afterward he enters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the bathroom theme of the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a סעודת קבע, walk forty אמות, relieve yourself, then enter.

steps.title: Removing תפילין before a set meal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that someone going in to a סעודת קבע takes off his תפילין first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: one who goes in to a set meal takes off his תפילין, and then goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יצחק about what to do with תפילין before a set meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A long, relaxed meal is not a fitting place to wear תפילין, so he removes them before entering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One who enters a set meal
removes his tefillin and afterward enters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another rule about preparing for a סעודת קבע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Take off your תפילין before entering a סעודת קבע.

steps.title: רבי חייא disagrees: place them on the table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יצחק disagrees with רבי חייא, who says one places his תפילין on his table, and that this is admirable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי חייא, for רבי חייא said: he places them on his table, and this is admirable for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יצחק's ruling clashes with another view, and quotes רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא holds that during the meal the תפילין are placed on his table, and calls this admirable. The גמרא labels the two views as a real disagreement about what one should do with תפילין at a set meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Admirable, a fine thing for him

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Chiya,
for Rabbi Chiya said:
he places them on his table,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means his תפילין, so they are right there and ready to put on again.

phrases.english: and so it is admirable for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יצחק's ruling is disputed by רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא: during a set meal, the תפילין are placed on his table, and this is admirable.

steps.title: Until when?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long during the meal this rule about the תפילין applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תפילין are not worn during the meal, we need to know at what point in the meal this stops.

phrases.english: And until when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit of the rule just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long into the meal the תפילין stay off.

steps.title: Until the time of the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: until the time of the ברכה, meaning ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: until the time of the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 19 with the opinion of רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תפילין stay off only until it is time to say the ברכה after the meal. From then on, the reason to keep them off no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of the blessing (ברכת המזון)

steps.whatToRemember: For a סעודת קבע: relieve yourself first, take off your תפילין (רבי חייא: place them on the table), and they stay off until it is time for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Until the time of the blessing.
phrases.notes: He means ברכת המזון, the blessing said after the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule lasts until the time of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Two teachings clash about wrapping תפילין with money
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows wrapping תפילין together with money in a head covering. Another ברייתא forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a person may wrap his תפילין with his money in his head covering. Another ברייתא teaches: he may not wrap them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side that seem to say opposite things. This sets up the question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources talk about the same act: wrapping תפילין and coins in one cloth. One says it is allowed and the other says it is not, so it looks like a real contradiction. The גמרא will need to show they are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A head covering, used here as a small wrapping cloth

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
A person may bundle his tefillin
with his money in his head covering.
And another baraita teaches: He may not bundle them.
phrases.notes: Same case as before, tefillin and money in one cloth. This time the answer is no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of תפילין during a meal to a new question about storing תפילין respectfully.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about wrapping תפילין with money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings about the same act, so it looks like they contradict each other.

steps.title: The answer: it depends whether the cloth was set aside for תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that forbids is talking about a cloth set aside for תפילין. The ברייתא that allows is talking about a cloth that was not set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This one is where he set the cloth aside for תפילין, and that one is where he did not set it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloth that was set aside (הזמנה) for תפילין gets a holy status, so coins may not go into it. The next step, from רב חסדא, adds that it must also have actually been used for them. A plain cloth that was never set aside has no such status, so תפילין and money may be wrapped in it together.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult, meaning there is no real contradiction
He set it aside, or designated it, for a purpose
Setting something aside for a specific use

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
this one is where he designated it,
phrases.notes: This first "this one" goes with the ברייתא that forbids.

phrases.english: that one is where he did not designate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא deals with a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to argue about the same cloth.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cloth set aside for תפילין may not hold money. A cloth not set aside may hold both.

steps.title: רב חסדא: setting aside and actual use are both needed
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a cloth becomes forbidden for coins only when it was set aside for תפילין and תפילין were actually wrapped in it. Either one alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: a תפילין cloth that a person set aside for wrapping תפילין, and he did wrap תפילין in it, may not be used for coins. If he set it aside but never wrapped תפילין in it, or wrapped תפילין in it without setting it aside, he may put money in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חסדא to support its answer that setting the cloth aside is what makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא makes the rule more exact. The cloth becomes forbidden only with both steps: setting it aside and actually using it. So the ברייתא that forbids is about a cloth that had both, and the ברייתא that allows covers every other case.
steps.confusionAlert: Setting the cloth aside alone does not forbid it according to רב חסדא. He needs both: it was set aside, and תפילין were actually wrapped in it.

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said:
This cloth of tefillin
that he designated to bundle tefillin in it,
and he did bundle tefillin in it,
it is forbidden to bundle coins in it.
If he designated it but did not bundle tefillin in it,
or he bundled tefillin in it but did not designate it,
it is permitted to bundle money in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 with an אמורא's ruling and makes it more exact.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that setting the cloth aside is the deciding factor
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling about the תפילין cloth

steps.title: How אביי would explain the rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that setting something aside counts by itself. So for him, a cloth set aside for תפילין is forbidden for money even if תפילין were never wrapped in it. Using it without setting it aside does not forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to אביי, who says that setting aside is significant: if he set the cloth aside, it is forbidden even though he never wrapped תפילין in it. If he wrapped תפילין in it, it is forbidden if he set it aside, and not forbidden if he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the rule would work for אביי, who disagrees with רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, both setting aside and use are needed. For אביי, setting aside (הזמנה) is enough on its own. Use without setting aside does nothing for either of them, so the only argument is about a cloth that was set aside but never used.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting aside is significant: it counts by itself

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: a cloth is forbidden for money only if it was set aside for תפילין AND used for them. אביי: setting aside alone is enough. Both agree that using it without setting it aside does not forbid it.

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, who said
designation is significant:

phrases.aramaic: אַזְמְנֵיהּ אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא צָר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: If he designated it, even though he did not bundle tefillin in it, it is forbidden.
If he bundled tefillin in it: if he designated it, it is forbidden;
if he did not designate it, it is not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אביי's version of the rule as an alternative to רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אביי, setting the cloth aside alone forbids putting money in it. Using it without setting it aside does not.

steps.title: May one sleep with תפילין under his head?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב נחוניא asks רב יהודה whether a person may put his תפילין under his head. He explains that under the feet is clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, the son of רב נחוניא, asked רב יהודה: may a person place his תפילין under his head? I am not asking about under his feet, because that treats them with disrespect. What I am asking about is under his head: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question about respect for תפילין: may they be placed under one's head, for example while sleeping?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The asker first says what he is not asking. Under the feet is clearly disrespectful, so it is forbidden. Under the head is less clear, so that is his real question.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him, a formal question put to a teacher
A disrespectful way of treating something
I am not asking about this, it is obvious to me

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked
the son of Rav Nechunya, of Rav Yehuda:
What is the law: may a person place his tefillin
under his head?

phrases.aramaic: תַּחַת מַרְגְּלוֹתָיו לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: About under his feet I have no question,
since that treats them disrespectfully.
What I am asking about
is under his head: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּנְיָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about respect for תפילין, separate from the cloth discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether placing תפילין under one's head counts as disrespect

steps.title: שמואל: it is allowed, even with his wife
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers in the name of שמואל that placing תפילין under one's head is allowed, even if his wife is with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what שמואל said: it is permitted, even if his wife is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by quoting his teacher שמואל: it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the head is not a disrespectful place like under the feet, so it is allowed. שמואל goes further and allows it even when his wife is with him in bed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that respect for תפילין depends on where they are placed. Under the head is respectful enough, and under the feet is not.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
It is permitted, even if his wife is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing תפילין under one's head is allowed, even if his wife is with him.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids תפילין under the head when the wife is present
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא. It allows תפילין under the head but forbids it when his wife is with him, unless there is a spot three טפחים higher or lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected from a ברייתא: A person should not put his תפילין under his feet, because that treats them with disrespect. But he may put them under his head. If his wife is with him, it is forbidden. If there is a spot three טפחים higher or lower, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that clashes with שמואל's ruling from Step 26. שמואל allowed it even with his wife present, but the ברייתא forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with שמואל on the basic point: under the head is fine and under the feet is not. The clash is only about when his wife is with him. שמואל said it is allowed, and the ברייתא says it is forbidden. The ברייתא also gives a way out: a spot three טפחים away counts as a separate place.

keyTerms.meaning: A disrespectful way of treating something holy
Three handbreadths, a set distance in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not argue with שמואל about putting תפילין under the head in general. Both allow that. The only conflict is the case where his wife is with him.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A person should not place his tefillin
under his feet,
because he treats them in a disrespectful way,
but he may place them under his head.
And if his wife was with him, it is forbidden.
If there was a place three handbreadths higher
or three handbreadths lower, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling quoted by רב יהודה in Step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that תפילין may go under the head even when his wife is with him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly forbids exactly the case שמואל permitted, when his wife is with him.

steps.title: שמואל is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the ברייתא refutes שמואל, and it confirms that the refutation stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of שמואל. Yes, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits there is no answer for שמואל. The ברייתא wins the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered to rescue שמואל. The repeated word confirms that the challenge stands. This sets up רבא's surprising ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a decisive challenge that has no answer

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Shmuel,
it is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the challenge in Step 27 defeats שמואל
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא refutes שמואל's ruling that allows it with his wife present.

steps.title: רבא rules like שמואל despite the refutation
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even though a ברייתא refuted שמואל, the הלכה still follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even though a ברייתא was taught that refutes שמואל, the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a surprising ruling. Practical הלכה goes with שמואל even though he was just refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a refuted opinion is not followed. רבא makes an exception here and keeps שמואל's lenient ruling as the practical הלכה. This raises an obvious question about why, which the גמרא asks next.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a refutation in the גמרא does not always decide the practical הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּתַנְיָא
phrases.english: Rava said: Even though it was taught in a ברייתא
a refutation of Shmuel,
the halakha follows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּתַנְיָא תְּיוּבְתָּא דִשְׁמוּאֵל, הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules in practice for שמואל, even after the refutation in Step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows שמואל: one may put תפילין under his head even when his wife is with him.

steps.title: Why rule like a refuted opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא follows שמואל. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question comes straight from the tension in Step 29. A refuted opinion would not normally be followed, so a reason is needed. The answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's ruling in Step 29
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the הלכה follows שמואל even though a ברייתא refuted him
